_frozen: 2026-10-21, before any variant was designed or built. Folded in Zach's two mid-round constraints (plugins for any manufacturer; always within reach and small) before freezing. Do not edit after variants exist; amend visibly instead.
name: IO diagnostics

amendments.quote: It should be easy to extend with any new sensors from any manufacturer in the future, so it should likely follow a plugin-like system. ... I want something always within reach and small.
amendments.effect: fr2 (plugins, 25%) and fr3 (always within reach, 20%) were written from this; a standalone app only as what the top-bar surface opens.

amendments.when: 2026-10-21 ~19:00, AFTER the freeze, before any variant was finished (one host was half-built and was rebuilt on this)
amendments.quote: For each of our sensors we are already building associated digital models, drivers, Python SDKs, etc. We can just leverage the exact same code. ... simple things like reset, view the configuration, etc. You plug in a device and want to see that it's plugged in, what its ID is, what its version is, whether a software update is needed... just checking basic communications, comms speed, etc. We don't need any complex robot control software.

fr2.name: Drivers bring their own diagnostics
fr2.passCondition: The plugin IS the device's own driver/SDK package (moteus_servo, intel_rgbd, obsbot_ptz_camera) exposing a small diagnostics entry point; IO diagnostics only discovers devices and calls it. Adding a manufacturer = adding that entry point plus a USB matcher to its driver package: zero host or UI edits, no parallel per-device code, the hardware gate inherited.

anchors.1: Per-device code lives in IO diagnostics, duplicating what the driver already knows.
anchors.3: Drivers expose it, but the host still needs per-type glue or UI work, or the contract shuts out non-Python vendor tools.
anchors.5: A driver entry point plus a matcher, nothing else; proven by a test that points the host at a driver and sees it discovered.

fr4.name: Truthful diagnostics before the stack runs
fr4.passCondition: Per device: presence, identity and ids, firmware and driver version, update available, read-only config, and a comms check (latency, loss, bus error counters, link speed); adapter, bus and node kept separate; every value carries its source and age; blocked shows who holds the port or the lock.

anchors.1: One undifferentiated status, or a stale value shown as live.
anchors.3: Identity and comms are shown, but versions, update or config are missing, or provenance is partial.
anchors.5: Every item is present with provenance; adapter, bus and node separated; CAN 15's fault named with when it occurs; blocked says who and shows the last known value with its age.

g2.addition: Reset and config writes are the only state-changing actions: explicit, per device, user-initiated, confirmed, and still gated (never while the port is held or the rack bus lock is taken). Nothing does motion or control.

amendments.fixture: Adds the post-restart frame (~19:00): 272813EF present with no board answering (motor supply off), 28B3A25D gone, both D405s present. The 18:11-18:25 frames stay as the other states.

outcome: Plug a sensor, actuator or bus adapter into the rack PC and see it appear in the top bar within seconds: what it is, what is on it (bus ids) and whether it is healthy, without ever disturbing hardware an experiment is using.

requirements.name: Plug it in, see it appear
requirements.why: Zach's literal ask: "I just want to plug stuff in and see it pop up." Today's 28B3A25D flapped four times on port 1-7 in 17 s before settling on 1-5, so a pop-up per USB enumeration is noise.
requirements.passCondition: Within about 2 s of a settled plug the device appears on the top-bar surface with a notice that takes no focus; a flapping device yields one coalesced notice; unplug and re-enumeration are visible too.

anchors.1: The device shows up only when the surface is next opened or polled, or every enumeration fires its own pop-up.
anchors.3: It appears promptly, but the notice is generic or a flap produces several notices.
anchors.5: One specific, coalesced notice ("28B3A25D plugged, 0 boards answer") within seconds; unplug and the D405's 4 s drop are visible as events.

requirements.name: New device types are plugins
requirements.why: Zach, mid-round 2026-10-21: "It should be easy to extend with any new sensors from any manufacturer in the future, so it should likely follow a plugin-like system."
requirements.passCondition: Adding a new manufacturer's device type (worked example: Robotiq 2F-85 on its FTDI USB-RS485 adapter, Modbus id 9) is one plugin unit implementing a small contract (passive match, children, health), discovered without editing the core or the UI; the UI renders it generically and the hardware gate is inherited, not re-implemented.

anchors.1: A new device type needs edits to the core or the UI.
anchors.3: One plugin unit, but the UI or the gating needs per-type work, or the contract shuts out vendor tools (one language, one process).
anchors.5: One small unit, zero core or UI edits, gating inherited, proven by a test that drops it in and sees the device discovered.

requirements.name: Always within reach, one calm answer
requirements.why: Zach, mid-round: "something always within reach and small"; a standalone app only as what the small surface opens. His calm-UI rule: the first screen answers "is it OK, what needs me?" and detail is pulled, not pushed.
requirements.passCondition: The top-bar presence stays small and quiet when all is well, shows an exception cue when something needs him, and one click gives a first screen whose headline answers OK / what needs me, with ids and detail one more click deeper.

anchors.1: A dense first screen, or a separate app is the primary surface.
anchors.3: A small top-bar presence, but the first screen pushes everything at once or the cue is ambiguous.
anchors.5: A quiet icon, a clear exception cue, the headline answer first and detail by progressive disclosure.

requirements.name: Truthful bus health
requirements.why: Health has layers and contention. 28B3A25D's adapter is fine while its bus is dead (error-passive, nobody ACKs); CAN 15 is quiet at idle but trips fault 33 on bridge enable; a busy bus is not a broken bus.
requirements.passCondition: Each bus shows the ids that answer (against the expected count when known); adapter, bus and node health are separate (err/warn/tdc, fault codes with names and when they occur); every value carries its source and age (live, last known from the inventory, reported by the running experiment, or blocked by a named holder).

anchors.1: One undifferentiated status, or a stale value shown as live.
anchors.3: Ids and faults are shown, but the layers merge or provenance is partial.
anchors.5: Adapter, bus and node are separate; CAN 15's fault is named with when it occurs; blocked shows who holds the bus plus the last known value and its age.

requirements.name: Names other tools can use
requirements.why: Inferred (from the coordinator, not Zach): /dev/fdcanusb now points at the newest adapter, the dead bus, so scripts that default to it go wrong. The rack session runner could resolve adapters by serial instead.
requirements.passCondition: Serial-keyed identity with the by-id path, the /dev/fdcanusb trap surfaced, and a machine-readable snapshot a script can read.

anchors.3: Serial-keyed and the trap is shown, but there is no machine-readable output.
anchors.5: Serial-keyed, trap surfaced, and a versioned machine-readable snapshot that a real example script consumes.

requirements.name: Stock parts, small to keep alive
requirements.why: Zach's off-the-shelf-first rule: reuse GNOME's own UI, AppIndicator, libnotify, udev, the repo's detection code and the Claude Hub tray where they fit. Every always-on process or shell extension is maintenance and upgrade risk.
requirements.passCondition: Thin glue over stock parts, few new always-on processes, low risk of breaking his session on a GNOME upgrade.

anchors.1: A bespoke stack with shell-crash or upgrade risk and new daemons.
anchors.3: Mostly stock, with one notable custom piece.
anchors.5: Thin glue over stock parts, at most one small process, upgrade-safe.

hardGates.name: Never steals focus
hardGates.why: No window raise and no app activation. A plug-in pop-up must be a non-focus-stealing notification or a top-bar cue (enforced on his machine by the no-focus-steal hook).

hardGates.name: Never interferes with hardware in use
hardGates.why: Detection is passive by default (sysfs, /dev/serial/by-id, USB descriptors, /proc). An active check (a CAN query, a camera open) runs only when no process holds the port AND the rack bus lock is free; it is query-only with an outer timeout. "Blocked because the bus is busy" is a shown state, not an error.

hardGates.name: Prototype only
hardGates.why: Nothing installed system-wide, no change to his GNOME settings, no shell extension enabled in his session, no udev rules. Prototypes run from the repo or render in the gallery.

invariants: Top-bar first: a small presence that is always within reach; any larger window is only what it opens.

Same fixture in every variant: today's real plug of 28B3A25D (4 flaps, then settled), the per-bus id lists, a blocked health check, CAN 15's fault 33, 28B3A25D's dead bus, the /dev/fdcanusb trap, and a Robotiq 2F-85 added through a plugin.
Passive detection only in this round: no CAN adapter or camera is opened (the orchestrator is running rack experiments on them).
Reuse the repo's detection code (find_port_holders, camera_holders, the inventory snapshot, moteus_find_ids / can_bus_triage for the gated active path) rather than rewriting it.
